newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt rises, tightens to U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt rises, tightens to U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Emerging market debt rose solidly on Tuesday and spreads over U.S. Treasuries narrowed after market-friendly U.S. economic data, traders said.
May construction spending data and a report by the National Association of Purchasing Management prompted a runup in Treasuries, spurring a similar reaction in emerging market bonds, they said.
"Treasuries a couple of days ago really gave people a scare," one trader said. "We've since recovered from that, and that's primarily what's driving our market."
Trading activity remained light, market experts said.
Among major Latin American issues, Brazil "C" bonds climbed 5/8 to 81, Mexico pars rose 3/4 to 78-1/8 and Argentina FRBs were 1/8 higher at 94-1/8.

Spreads narrowed in most countries, but nowhere more than in Ecuador. Ecuador PDIs rebounded 1-1/2 to 66 and tightened about 35 basis points, making up some of the ground lost over the past several days.
Trading was confined mainly to Wall Street dealers, with spotty client buying, traders said.

President Fabian Alarcon said Monday evening that he expected Finance Minister Carlos Davalos to remain at his post until July 25. But he said Ecuador's central bank and monetary board leadership would remain intact.
Traders said Alarcon's announcement lent support to the country's Brady debt.

"Ecuador's been doing very well on the news that there may be no further resignations," one trader said. "Supposedly ... Alarcon has agreed to meet (the economic team's) needs in terms of making fiscal change."
In addition, central bank chief Fidel Jaramillo said a mission of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) would visit Ecuador early this month to evaluate the economy.
Bulgaria debt rose as the government launched its currency board system that pegs the lev to the mark. Bulgaria FLIRBs BGFLIRB=RR jumped 1-5/8 to 58-1/2.
But traders said volume had been low, with perhaps $20 million of FLIRBs, IABs and discounts traded altogether.
On Wednesday at about 1400 EDT/1800 GMT, the U.S. Federal Reserve will announce the results of its policy meeting. U.S. analysts in a Reuters poll unanimously projected no change in interest rates.
